findings.claim: An acknowledgement for a frame id never sent to that client can poison the connection's monotonic ack watermark and wedge ack-paced delivery until pacing is switched back to push.
findings.evidence: Against the release binary and real Chrome, after ack opt-in an ack for seq 1000000000000 released one frame (936), but acking the actually sent 936 released no further frame for 700 ms; switching to push immediately resumed frames. reader_loop retains the maximum arbitrary client seq at websocket.rs:487-499, and the writer accepts acked >= awaiting at 410-420.
findings.path: reader_loop ack.send_if_modified -> ack_rx watermark -> awaiting_ack release guard

findings.claim: Ack pacing does not bound a newly connected client to one frame in flight because the cached seed frame bypasses the pacing state machine.
findings.evidence: Five immediate opt-in connections each received two frames before sending any ack: [431,432], [477,478], [523,524], [570,571], [616,617]. websocket.rs:341-346 sends the cached frame before the writer initializes awaiting_ack at line 359 and observes config.
findings.path: handle_ws_client cached seed send -> writer pacing initialization

findings.claim: Interleaved config updates can be coalesced by the watch channel, so a transient switch to push that should release an outstanding frame can be lost before the writer observes it.
findings.evidence: With a held ack-paced frame, sending pacing=push immediately followed by pacing=ack failed to advance the stream in 9 of 10 real-Chrome trials. config.send_replace stores only the latest ClientConfig and config_rx.changed reads only the final state, so the line 404-407 release action for push is skipped.
findings.path: reader_loop config.send_replace -> watch coalescing -> writer config_rx.changed

findings.claim: The new test named to guard the uncapped default does not fail when the default is changed to 1 fps.
findings.evidence: Temporarily initializing ClientConfig with max_fps=1 left test_uncapped_client_receives_consecutive_frames green in 1.01 s because the test has no elapsed-time assertion; therefore the regression guard at mod.rs:830-851 does not prove uncapped behavior.

findings.claim: The new core skill falsely promises that ordered status, tabs, url, and console messages are never dropped.
findings.evidence: With a real ack-paced TCP client paused, emitting 200 distinct 20 KB console events and resuming yielded only 82 marks; marks 20 onward were missing in a contiguous lag window. websocket.rs:379-380 explicitly continues on broadcast RecvError::Lagged, contradicting skill-data/core/references/streaming.md:59.
findings.layer: documented protocol through real TCP transport
findings.path: broadcast console channel -> lagged receiver -> dropped events

findings.claim: The new core skill says out-of-range maxFps values are ignored, but values above 120 are clamped to 120.
findings.evidence: apply_config uses fps.min(120) at websocket.rs:35, and the committed test test_parse_config_max_fps_clamps_without_wrapping asserts 500 becomes 120; skill-data/core/references/streaming.md:74 says out-of-range values are ignored. Live Chrome also distinguished maxFps=5 (10 frames/2s) from maxFps=500 (186 frames/2s, approximately the 120 cap under production rate).
findings.path: core streaming reference -> apply_config maxFps parser

dogfood.substrate: real Chrome with a CSS compositor animation
observations: Push delivered 206 frames in 2.2 seconds; maxFps=5 delivered 10 frames in 2 seconds.
Frame timestamps were nonzero epoch milliseconds and seq increased from 570 to 571 across stream disable/enable.
Out-of-order stale acks did not release a held frame; reconnect reset per-client state; simultaneous clients retained independent pacing.
Input clicked the real DOM while an ack-paced frame was held and while a raw client had paused reads for 5 seconds.
Future unsent ack, opening-seed pacing, config coalescing, and ordered-channel loss were reproduced as described in F1, F2, F3, and F5.

prior_runs.verdict: Confirms its IdleActivity placement and merged maxFps/input findings; retains its passive-client idle-timeout issue candidate as out of scope. It predated ack pacing and therefore missed F1-F7.

Its opening-write, transport-buffer, and missing-core-doc findings were valid at d86d230 but are refuted by the current branch's reader ordering, opt-in ack mode, and core docs. It necessarily missed the new ack-state and new-doc defects F1-F7.
